clues.text: Solomon asked Hiram king of Tyre to have cedars cut down here for building the temple.
Solomon sent his forced laborers here in monthly shifts of 10,000 men, one month away and two at home.
Solomon built a great hall with four rows of cedar pillars and named it for the forest of this place.
Before he died, Moses begged God to let him cross the Jordan and see the good hill country and this land.
A psalm says the voice of the LORD makes this place skip like a calf, and Sirion like a young wild ox.
In Solomon's song, the groom calls his bride to come with him from here, down from Amana, Senir and Hermon.
Sennacherib king of Assyria boasted that his chariots climbed its remote peaks and cut down its tallest cedars.
